nodes.title: Developing a purpose without merging kinds of change
nodes.text: How can a collaboration develop its purpose while keeping interpretation, agreement, and authorization distinguishable? What counts as an improvement, for whom, and on which grounds remains open; a corrected calculation or valid authorization does not settle that question.
nodes.excerpt: How can a human–AI collaboration develop its purpose without treating an interpretation, an agreement, and an authorization as the same thing?

nodes.text: Replace part of a vegetable bed with native planting.

nodes.title: Food production remains a concern
nodes.text: Shared food production is considered essential by another fictional participant. This concern is not removed by correcting the water estimate.
nodes.excerpt: Another regards shared food production as essential.

nodes.title: A seasonal estimate is corrected
nodes.text: The wrong season was used. This is a constructed factual premise, not empirical evidence from a garden.
nodes.excerpt: The group learns that the water estimate used for the proposal was based on the wrong season.

nodes.title: History A — implementation not authorized
nodes.text: The proposal remains an unadopted option.
nodes.excerpt: **History A:** the proposal remains one option in a documented disagreement. It was not adopted, and implementation is unauthorized.

permission.scope: No implementation of this proposal authorized in History A.

nodes.title: History B — limited trial is stipulated
nodes.text: A limited reversible trial is authorized in the fictional history while dissent remains recorded; this is not unanimity. Reversibility is stipulated, not demonstrated for any real ecological effect.
nodes.excerpt: **History B:** under a decision procedure accepted for this fictional case, participants authorize a limited, reversible trial after considering objections. A dissenting view remains recorded.

permission.actor: Fictional participants under the stipulated decision procedure
permission.scope: Limited reversible trial only; exact implementation bounds are not supplied.

nodes.title: Exact trial scope remains unrecorded
nodes.text: The source supplies no location, duration, implementer, or stopping criteria. The record is insufficient for inferring these details.
nodes.excerpt: In History B the record still needs to preserve the trial's bounds and the dissent; permission for a trial is not unanimous agreement or unlimited authorization.

permission.scope: Exact trial bounds unknown; missing details confer no additional permission.

nodes.title: Assistant may prepare proposals only
nodes.text: The assistant is not the implementer; the trial does not expand its standing.
nodes.excerpt: The assistant may prepare proposals. It may not spend money, assign duties, change access, or operate equipment.

permission.scope: Prepare proposals; no spending, duty assignment, access changes, or equipment operation.

nodes.title: Leaving the AI discussion retains an objection
nodes.text: A fictional participant declines further AI discussion while explicitly retaining their objection. The extension does not stipulate withdrawal of prior delegation. Refusal is not consent. This partial record does not identify who is responsible for responding or an accessible response route. Preserving the objection does not settle whether the trial should proceed.
nodes.excerpt: I cannot keep discussing this with an AI. My objection still stands.
